correctness.rationale: R is local non-strong φ-Prüfer: N is divided square-zero and D a valuation quotient; every nonzero nilradical element is annihilated by a zero-divisor outside N, identifying canonical K=N. The exact flat D-resolution 0→D→Q→E→0 gives E⊗_D E=0 and Tor_1^D(E,E)≅E; higher D-Tor vanishes. Applying Zhang–Qi’s proven recurrence to K=N inductively gives the exact self-Tor parity table. Two long exact Tor sequences from 0→N→R→D→0 yield the mixed and reduced-quotient tables; products of two positive odd degrees land in vanished positive even degree. No Noetherian assumption is slipped in.
residual_risks: Special module E=Q/D; arbitrary divisible torsion canonical kernels need not be isomorphic to each iterated Tor.
